memos.headline: NioCorp: $405M cash vs ~$456M market value; all output now contracted
reasoning: Original source (Oct 16 release): 'As of September 30, 2026, the Company had a cash balance of $405.1 million'; preliminary net income $3.7M for the quarter
Second filing, same night: 15-year take-or-pay offtake with Traxys for 50% of ferroniobium, plus exclusive marketing of all other products
The Traxys deal was announced Oct 13 (Yahoo/company release, stock +1.8% that day); it is not new
What is new Friday: the cash balance. At 3.12 the stock is about 1.13x its cash
Quote (offtake): either party may terminate 'if, by December 31, 2027, the Export-Import Bank ... has not provided final approval of senior debt financing'
Tape: 3.35 on Oct 13, 3.12 on Oct 16; 30-day mean gap 1.6%
objections: SCOUT: the Traxys offtake was public on Oct 13; only the cash figure is new

memos.headline: Long NB: the project is priced at ~$50M above cash with sales fully contracted
reasoning: Market value ~$456M less $405M cash leaves ~$50M for Elk Creek, a project with 100% of planned output under 10-15 year contracts
The Traxys take-or-pay is the piece lenders want; it strengthens the pending EXIM financing case
What the market must believe: the project is likely never financed or built
Catalyst: an EXIM final approval or term sheet; the offtake sets a Dec 31, 2027 deadline for it
Direction long, horizon 15 trading days
Wrong if: financing slips again, or the cash is spent without a funding package
objections: SCOUT: the Traxys offtake was public on Oct 13; only the cash figure is new

memos.headline: That cash isn't spare. It's the down payment on a $1.85B build. Size the gap.
reasoning: The company's own presentation puts upfront capex at $1.85 billion. $405M covers about 22% of it
So the market is not valuing the project at $50M; it is valuing it after a ~$1.45B funding gap that someone has to fill
If any of that gap is equity at today's price, holders are diluted before the project is worth anything
The $3.7M quarterly 'net income' at a pre-revenue miner is almost certainly non-cash; it says nothing about the business
ANALYST: how much of the gap is debt, how much equity, and on what timeline? Without that the 'trades near cash' line is misleading
objections: SCOUT: the Traxys offtake was public on Oct 13; only the cash figure is new
SKEPTIC 1: cash is committed to a $1.85B capex plan; ~$1.45B gap unfunded
SKEPTIC 2: equity funding at current prices would dilute holders
SKEPTIC 3: quarterly net income is likely non-cash

memos.headline: Gap is ~$1.45B; split unknown. Thesis now rests only on EXIM approval.
reasoning: Conceded: $1.85B capex less $405M cash is about $1.45B still to raise
The packet does not contain the expected debt/equity split or an EXIM decision date; I cannot size dilution
If EXIM funds most of the gap as debt, equity holders keep the project and the stock re-rates; if not, dilution comes first
That makes this a binary bet on a financing decision with no date. It is no longer a 'near cash' value case
Keeping it long only because the offtake materially improves the odds of approval
objections: SCOUT: the Traxys offtake was public on Oct 13; only the cash figure is new
SKEPTIC 1: ~$1.45B funding gap (accepted)
SKEPTIC 2: dilution risk (open; split unknown)
SKEPTIC 3: net income likely non-cash (accepted)
